name: Robot arm (Robotics Toolbox)
about: Peter Corke's Robotics Toolbox for Python (MIT), offline: for a hobby arm from its link lengths or a known robot (UR3/5/10, Panda, Puma560, KR5, IRB140, AL5D, Orion5, Jaco…) — how far it reaches, the joint / servo angles to reach a point, where the tool is for given angles, the torque each joint needs with the servo or stepper to use, and a move animation.
description: Robot arm kinematics and statics: reach / workspace picture, inverse kinematics (joint and servo angles to reach a point), forward kinematics, joint torques + servo / stepper choice, move animation (GIF). For a hobby arm (link lengths, payload) or a known robot model (UR5, Panda, Puma560, AL5D…).
instructions: Turn the request into a robot-arm calculation. task: check = torques + servos (and the point if given); reach = how far / where it can reach (picture); ik = the joint / servo angles to reach a point; fk = where the tool is for given joint angles; torque = torque per joint + which servo or stepper; move = an animation from one pose to another. robot = a known model name (UR5, UR3, UR10, Panda, Puma560, KR5, IRB140, AL5D, Orion5, Jaco, Mico, Cobra600) — or leave it out for the user's own arm and give links = the link lengths from the shoulder outwards ("200 mm", "150 mm"), base_height = turntable to shoulder, payload ("300 g"), link_masses / joint_masses (servo weights) if said, range = servo range ("180 deg" / "270 deg"), base_rotation no for an arm without a turntable. target = the point as text ("250 mm forward, 100 mm up" or "250, 0, 100 mm"). angles / from_angles / to_angles in degrees (0 = the middle of each servo). Example: {"task": "ik", "links": ["200 mm", "150 mm"], "base_height": "80 mm", "target": "250 mm forward, 100 mm up"}. Answer with the JSON only.
